newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Brash says conditions have eased too far.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Brash says conditions have eased too far.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand governor Don Brash said on Thursday that monetary conditions had eased too far.
He reiterated that desired monetary conditions had not changed since the release of the Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Statement last Friday -- 825 on the bank's Monetary Conditions Index.

"Against this background, actual monetary conditions have been too easy over recent days. We will be looking to see actual conditions settle closer to the announced desired levels", Brash said in a statement.
The MCI had fallen to about 753 prior to Brash's statement today, but quickly rose to 766.32, 59 basis points below the bank's desired level.
The bank said in its Monetary Policy Statement on Friday that it would tolerate a 50 basis point deviation either side of its desired level in the weeks following a major inflation projection.

On Wednesday, Brash appeared before Parliament's Finance and Expenditure Committee but did not stress the limits of the bank's comfort zone, which dealers said was taken as a tacit acceptance of the extent of the market's easing since the MPS.

At 1.20 p.m. (0120 GMT), 20 minutes after the surprise statement, the Monetary Conditions Index had risen to 767.58 from its 761.59 open, bringing conditions to 57 basis points softer than the RBNZ's desired level.

The kiwi dollar was quoted at US$0.6776/83 compared with US$0.6774/81 in early morning trade. On its Trade-Weighted Index the kiwi was at 66.44 against 66.47 at the open and 66.28 just before the announcement.
The 90-day bank bills were also sluggish in their response. They were at 7.07 percent from 7.03 percent at the open.
